title: I made a small physics-drop game for the browser. One run takes 5 minutes, no download, no account
author: mkhorne
selftext:
Hey! Over the last weeks I built Dropforge together with Claude Code, and I want to share it.

The game: you drop balls into a peg board and collect points. Between drops you pick one of three upgrades and build the board out. The score goal grows every stage, so at some point every run ends. There is a daily board (same for everyone) and a mode where you place every peg yourself.

How we worked: I played the game every day and reported what felt wrong. Claude wrote the code, but more important, it measured things before changing them. It built a bot that plays thousands of runs, so balance changes were based on numbers, not gut feeling. When players said "my run got cancelled", we found the real cause together (a deploy invalidated running games) and fixed the system, not the symptom.

Free, works on phones: https://dropforge.unikhorne.dev

Still a solo project (well, solo plus AI). If you stop playing, tell me why. That helps the most.

comments.author: jscj1994
comments.body: A fun experiment for you to practice gamedev and vibecoding for sure. In terms of a game I'd play? Not really. This game exists in 1000s of forms already and is nothing new or special.
